across_options.issue: Beyond field placement, Header band enlarges Offered $38 and Listed at $45 relative to the base. Counter is also slightly wider, shifting the More control. These change type hierarchy and control geometry while D5 is being compared (ledger A3; constitution Article 14.4). Moving the action row onto white is an intended placement consequence, not separate drift.

Whole moment also changes texture: the faint curves visible in the base become effectively invisible, including on the unchanged left offer card. This does not isolate the Where choice from the Texture choice (ledger D5; constitution Article 14.4). The larger right field and square outer edges belong to the intended placement change.

The texture variants also change the field's color distribution, especially the stronger yellow lower-right corner in Strong lines. Curve direction and spacing change alongside line strength. The card edges, phone outlines and lower row contents shift slightly between renders. These are not pure changes of texture strength (constitution Article 14.4).

The visible item identities, prices, deadlines, action labels, Live and Draft pills, wordmark placement and navigation remain consistent. These are Today screens, so the list rows do not violate ledger L12's Sell-grid requirement. The More glyph supplies a visible third action; its contents cannot be assessed from these boards.
D5 explicitly permits the whole ground to exceed one third. B8 is therefore not used to fail this option. The permission does not waive the other brand ends or grouping rules.

Article 13 review: meaningful state pills, actual item subjects, plain copy and the specified palette do not establish an AI-tell cluster. Generic rounded cards alone are insufficient to fail B25. No supplied no-brand comparison establishes three matching axes. Per Part IV, source-dependent B13, B15, B22 and B27 are not applicable to these raster-only boards; font identity, exact weights, icon provenance and locale code are not inferred. Motion, menu behavior, photo provenance and exact token compliance remain unverified. The numbered callouts, connecting arrow and dotted connector are treated as review annotations, not app UI.
